question: How long is a Texas vessel registration valid before it must be renewed?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: It never expires once issued
explanation: A Texas boat registration is valid for two years from the date it is issued, after which it must be renewed to remain current.
source_note: TPWD Title, Registration, Tax & ID Requirements -- Registration Requirements

question: How early before its expiration date can a Texas vessel registration be renewed?
choice_a: Only on the exact day it expires
choice_b: Renewal is never allowed before expiration
choice_c: As early as 90 days prior to the expiration date
choice_d: As early as one full year prior to expiration
explanation: TPWD allows a boat owner to renew a Texas vessel registration as early as 90 days before it is set to expire.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- renewal timing

question: A vessel already registered and titled in another state is visiting Texas. How long may it operate on Texas water under its current out-of-state registration before Texas registration or tax obligations apply?
choice_a: Up to 10 consecutive days
choice_b: Indefinitely, as long as the owner does not become a Texas resident
choice_c: Out-of-state vessels may never operate on Texas water without first titling in Texas
choice_d: Up to 90 consecutive days
explanation: A vessel currently registered or titled in another state may operate in Texas for up to 90 consecutive days before Texas registration and use tax requirements come into play.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- out-of-state vessels

question: What option does TPWD offer to a boater who brings a vessel into Texas and wants to defer paying the full use tax while operating during the 90-day out-of-state window?
choice_a: A temporary use tax permit, at a fee of $150.00 per vessel or outboard motor, valid for the 90-day period
choice_b: Texas has no such permit; the full tax is always due immediately on arrival with no alternative
choice_c: A permanent tax waiver for any vessel that has ever been registered in another state
choice_d: A one-time $10 administrative fee that waives all future Texas use tax on that vessel
explanation: TPWD offers a temporary use tax permit for $150.00 per vessel or outboard motor, covering the 90-day period an out-of-state vessel may operate in Texas before use tax is otherwise due.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- temporary use tax permit

question: What is the Texas sales/use tax rate applied to the purchase of a taxable boat or outboard motor?
choice_a: 10% of the sales price
choice_b: 6.25% of the sales price
choice_c: 3% of the sales price
choice_d: There is no sales tax on boats or motors in Texas
explanation: Texas applies a 6.25% tax rate to the sales price of a taxable boat or outboard motor, collected by TPWD (or the Comptroller) at the time of titling or registration.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ / Texas Comptroller -- boat and boat motor tax rate

question: Is there a cap on the amount of Texas sales tax that can be charged on a single boat sale?
choice_a: No, there has never been any cap on Texas boat sales tax
choice_b: Yes, the cap is exactly $1,000 no matter the boat's price
choice_c: Yes -- the total boat sales tax collected on a single sale of a taxable boat cannot exceed $18,750, though this cap does not apply to an outboard motor sold with it
choice_d: The cap applies only to outboard motors, never to the boat itself
explanation: Texas law caps the boat sales tax collected on a single sale of a taxable boat at $18,750; an outboard motor sold along with the boat is taxed separately at 6.25% without this cap.
source_note: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts -- boat and boat motor sales and use tax

question: Within how many working days of a purchase (for purchases made on or after September 1, 2019) must a buyer submit the required title/registration application and pay tax to TPWD to avoid penalties?
choice_a: 5 working days
choice_b: 180 working days
choice_c: There is no deadline as long as the buyer eventually applies
choice_d: 45 working days
explanation: For a vessel or outboard motor purchased (or brought into Texas) on or after September 1, 2019, the buyer must file the required application and pay tax within 45 working days of the sale or arrival date to avoid penalties and interest.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- tax and title filing deadline

question: When selling a Texas-titled vessel or outboard motor, what must the seller do as part of the transfer?
choice_a: Complete the tax affidavit on the application, sign and date the original title, and list the buyer's name and address on the back of the title
choice_b: Nothing; TPWD automatically updates ownership records without any seller action
choice_c: Physically surrender the vessel's HIN plate to TPWD
choice_d: Re-register the vessel in their own name a second time before the sale is valid
explanation: A seller transferring a Texas-titled vessel or motor must complete the tax affidavit on the application form, sign and date the original title, and record the buyer's name and address on the back of the title.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- ownership transfer, seller obligations

question: After buying a used vessel in Texas, what must the buyer submit to TPWD, and within what timeframe, to complete the ownership transfer without penalty?
choice_a: Nothing is required from the buyer; only the seller has any filing obligation
choice_b: The assigned title, a completed application, serial number verification, required fees, and applicable tax, all within 45 days
choice_c: Only a verbal notification to a TPWD game warden
choice_d: A police report describing the sale
explanation: The buyer of a used vessel must submit the assigned title, a completed application, serial number verification, the required fees, and any applicable tax to TPWD within 45 days of the purchase to complete the transfer without penalty.
source_note: TPWD Registration and Titles FAQ -- ownership transfer, buyer obligations

question: Which category of U.S. Coast Guard-documented vessels is exempt from Texas state registration because of the vessel's length alone?
choice_a: Documented vessels shorter than 26 feet
choice_b: All documented sailboats, regardless of length
choice_c: Documented vessels exceeding 115 feet in length
choice_d: No documented vessel is ever exempt from Texas registration based on length
explanation: Among USCG-documented vessels, those exceeding 115 feet in length are exempt from Texas state registration, along with commercial tugboats and certain pilot/crew boats servicing cargo ships or offshore oil infrastructure.
source_note: TPWD Title, Registration, Tax & ID Requirements -- Registration Requirements, USCG-documented vessel exemptions

question: Besides large documented vessels over 115 feet, which other categories of USCG-documented vessels are specifically exempt from Texas state registration?
choice_a: Any documented vessel used for recreational fishing tournaments
choice_b: Any documented vessel owned by a Texas resident for more than 10 years
choice_c: Houseboats used exclusively on inland lakes
choice_d: Commercial tugboats, and pilot or crew boats transporting freight, supplies, or personnel to or from cargo ships, freighters, or offshore oil infrastructure
explanation: Texas exempts USCG-documented commercial tugboats and documented pilot or crew boats that transport freight, supplies, or personnel to or from cargo ships, freighters, or offshore oil infrastructure, from state registration.
source_note: TPWD Title, Registration, Tax & ID Requirements -- Registration Requirements, USCG-documented vessel exemptions

question: Which state agency is responsible for titling and registering vessels and outboard motors in Texas, rather than the county tax assessor-collector's motor vehicle office that titles cars?
choice_a: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD)
choice_b: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)
choice_c: Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)
choice_d: Texas General Land Office (GLO)
explanation: Unlike car titling, which runs through the county tax assessor-collector and TxDMV, Texas boat and outboard motor titling and registration is administered by TPWD, though some county tax offices act as agents for these transactions.
source_note: TPWD boat ownership program overview

question: What is TORA, the online tool TPWD provides related to vessel ownership?
choice_a: A mobile app for reporting boating accidents
choice_b: An online tool to query/look up boat ownership and titling records
choice_c: The online exam portal for the mandatory boater education course
choice_d: A tool for reserving campsites at state parks
explanation: TORA is TPWD's online system that lets the public query Texas boat ownership and title records.
source_note: TPWD Boating -- Ownership Inquiry (TORA) online tool

question: What can a Texas boat owner do using TPWD's online BORA system?
choice_a: File a mandatory boating accident report
choice_b: Schedule a game warden vessel safety inspection
choice_c: Renew or replace their vessel registration online
choice_d: Apply for a Party Boat Operator License
explanation: BORA is TPWD's online system for boat owners to renew or replace their Texas vessel registration.
source_note: TPWD Boating -- Renew/Replace Online (BORA) tool

question: What resource does TPWD maintain that lists vessels and outboard motors that have been abandoned in Texas?
choice_a: TPWD does not track abandoned vessels or motors in any way
choice_b: A private insurance-industry database unrelated to TPWD
choice_c: The list is maintained only by individual county sheriffs, never by TPWD
choice_d: An Abandoned Boats/Outboard Motors listing
explanation: TPWD publishes an Abandoned Boats/Outboard Motors listing as part of its boat ownership resources.
source_note: TPWD Boat Ownership -- Abandoned Boats/Outboard Motors Listing

question: TPWD publishes a summary booklet of Texas boating statutes on its official boating laws page under what title?
choice_a: The Water Safety Act
choice_b: The Texas Marine Code
choice_c: The Lake and River Safety Handbook
choice_d: The Coastal Boater's Statute Guide
explanation: TPWD's official boating laws page links to a downloadable summary of Texas boating statutes titled the Water Safety Act, covering vessel numbering, equipment, and operation requirements.
source_note: TPWD Boating Laws page -- Water Safety Act publication

question: Under Texas law, what generally defines a 'party boat' that requires its operator to hold a state Party Boat Operator License?
choice_a: Any privately owned vessel used to host a birthday party with friends aboard
choice_b: A vessel operated by the owner or an employee, rented or leased for a group recreational event, carrying more than six passengers and generally 30 feet or longer, excluding sailboats and certain other cases
choice_c: Any vessel under 16 feet used for fishing tournaments
choice_d: Any sailboat used for hire, regardless of passenger count
explanation: Texas defines a 'party boat' as a vessel operated by its owner or an employee, rented or leased for a group recreational event, carrying more than six passengers and generally at least 30 feet long, with sailboats and certain other cases excluded.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- definition of party boat

question: What is the minimum age to hold a Texas Party Boat Operator License?
choice_a: 16 years old
choice_b: 18 years old
choice_c: 21 years old
choice_d: 25 years old
explanation: An applicant for a Texas Party Boat Operator License must be at least 21 years old.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- eligibility requirements

question: Who is exempt from needing a Texas Party Boat Operator License even though they operate a qualifying party boat?
choice_a: Anyone who has operated boats for more than one year, regardless of any license
choice_b: Anyone who only operates on weekends
choice_c: No one is ever exempt from this license once a vessel qualifies as a party boat
choice_d: An operator who holds a USCG OUPV ('six-pack') license or higher
explanation: An operator who already holds a USCG Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels ('six-pack') license or a higher USCG credential does not need the separate Texas Party Boat Operator License.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- USCG OUPV exemption

question: What are the two ways an applicant can satisfy the experience requirement for a Texas Party Boat Operator License?
choice_a: A training path of 8 hours (4 observing, 4 operating) under a licensed operator while employed, or an experience path of 25 documented hours operating a party boat with no disqualifying violations
choice_b: There is no experience requirement at all, only the written exam
choice_c: Only by holding a commercial driver's license (CDL) for at least one year
choice_d: Only by completing 500 hours of open-water sailing
explanation: An applicant can satisfy the Party Boat Operator License experience requirement either through an 8-hour training path (4 hours observing, 4 hours operating) under a licensed operator while employed, or a 25-hour documented experience path operating a party boat with no disqualifying violations.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- experience/training paths

question: What is the format of the Part B examination required to obtain a Texas Party Boat Operator License?
choice_a: An unproctored 10-question online quiz with no minimum score
choice_b: A proctored exam of 50 questions with a 70% passing score
choice_c: A purely practical, on-water-only test with no written component
choice_d: A 200-question exam requiring a 90% passing score
explanation: The Part B examination for the Texas Party Boat Operator License is a proctored exam consisting of 50 questions, with a required passing score of 70%, scheduled through the TPWD Boater Education Office.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- Part B exam

question: What fee does TPWD charge for an original Texas Party Boat Operator License?
choice_d: There is no fee for the original license
explanation: TPWD charges $132 for an original Party Boat Operator License.
source_note: TPWD Party Boat Operator License Program -- license fee
